title: The Lives That 9/11 Keeps Taking
body_text:
In New York City this morning, the families of those killed at the World Trade Center on Sept. 11, 2001, will gather for the 25th time to honor the dead one by one.
Among those at ground zero will be an array of city officials who assured the public that it was safe to return to Lower Manhattan just weeks after the attacks.
Today, Sally Goldenberg, a reporter who covers politics and government for The New York Times, and Dana Nelson, who attended school next to ground zero, reveal the 9/11 health crisis that has now claimed more lives than the terrorist attacks themselves.
Guest: Sally Goldenberg, a reporter covering New York City politics and government for The New York Times.
Background reading: 

Documents suggest that New Yorkers were misled about air quality after 9/11.
